title: Introduce lightweight CI sequencer and dependency-signal cleaner
author: Nina Patel
release_notes: Introduces a small CI sequencer that orders lightweight preflight steps deterministically and a dependency-signal cleaner that reduces noise from transient dep updates. No customer-facing changes. Improves CI feedback time for small PRs by ~20%.
description:
Context and motivation: Our presubmit and lint pipelines have accumulated ad-hoc bootstrapping steps which slow down fast feedback and make small dependency churns noisy in CI telemetry. This PR introduces a lightweight CI sequencer component that consolidates lightweight preflight steps into a deterministically-ordered, cache-friendly execution path and a dependency-signal cleaner that suppresses spurious dep-change alerts (e.g., lockfile timestamp churn, auto-formatter tool bumps) while preserving signals for real upgrades.

What this PR does (single-line summary): Adds ci/sequencer.py (small orchestrator), refactors existing ci/bootstrap.* into ordered stages, and introduces tools/dep_signal_cleaner.py plus small lint/test wiring.

Design notes: The sequencer is intentionally minimal: it does not replace heavy presubmit orchestration, only the light-weight fastpath for quick feedback. It runs three stages: env-prepare (cache warm), quick-lint (fast linters + formatting check), and smoke (unit tests subset). Each stage reports structured exit codes for downstream telemetry. The dependency-signal cleaner is a post-commit hook run in CI that normalizes dependency metadata and emits a delta-summary; when the delta matches configured heuristics (timestamp-only or checksum-stable), it suppresses noisy alerts.

Checklist: 
- [x] Add sequencer implementation and minimal integration tests
- [x] Wire sequencer into lightweight CI lane (GH Actions composite)
- [x] Add dep-signal cleaner and heuristic rules
- [x] Update team CI docs with usage and opt-outs
- [x] Run small-scale dogfood on infra/canary and iterate

Commits (high-level): 
- 7e1a9b: initial sequencer skeleton and runner shim
- 4a2f3c: integrate sequencer into .github/workflows/fastpath.yml as a composite action call
- a9d44e: add dep_signal_cleaner utility and heuristics ruleset
- c12f80: add unit tests and small fixture lockfiles for cleaner testing
- d88b21: docs and examples, update team playbook

Changed files (high-level, illustrative): 
- ci/sequencer.py (new) - core orchestrator for fastpath lanes
- ci/steps/prepare_env.sh (moved/trimmed) - smaller, cache-friendly variant
- ci/steps/quick_lint.sh (new wrapper) - fast linters only
- tools/dep_signal_cleaner.py (new) - normalizes lockfile metadata and emits summary
- .github/workflows/fastpath.yml (updated) - invokes sequencer as composite action for fast feedback
- docs/ci/fastpath.md (updated) - usage and opt-out guidance
- tests/ci/test_sequencer.py (new) - unit tests for sequencing logic
- tests/tools/test_dep_cleaner.py (new) - fixture-driven tests for cleaner heuristics
- package.json / go.mod (small devdeps bumps) - pin a stable composite action helper

Review conversation (high-level snippets): 
- Ethan Morales (reviewer): "Overall looks clean. Two asks: make the sequencer idempotent across retries and add a short-circuit when cache hits make stages unnecessary."
- Nina (author): "Addressed: added retry-idempotency token and cache-hit short-circuit. See sequencer.py lines 78-108."
- Sofia Ivanov: "Dep cleaner heuristics look reasonable but add an allowlist for known formatter bumps (we see these every few weeks). Also please add a note on opt-out for repos that vendor lockfiles."
- Nina: "Added allowlist config and opt-out flag; documented in docs/ci/fastpath.md."
- Liam Chen: "CI job matrix logs look fine. One minor nit: prefer exit code 2 for suppressed-noise vs exit code 0 for success."
- Nina: "Switched suppressed-noise to exit code 2 and updated telemetry mapping."

CI summary during review: 
- Actions: fastpath.yml (composite call) -> lint (fast), unit-smoke, dep-cleaner-check
- Initial run: lint passed, unit-smoke flaky (1 failure) -> fixed by adding a small test fixture; rerun passed
- Integration run on infra/canary: green, overall run time for fastpath reduced from ~95s to ~75s on average (measured over 50 runs).

Risk and mitigations: 
- Risk: Dep-signal suppression could hide real upgrades. Mitigation: default heuristics are conservative and we added an allowlist/denylist and a telemetry mismatch alert if the cleaner suppresses >5% of dep deltas in a day. Additionally, the opt-out flag is available per-repo.
- Risk: Sequencer composite introduces new failure modes in GH Actions. Mitigation: keep legacy fastpath as fallback; sequencer-run is gated behind a feature flag (repo-level) for the first week and can be toggled via org config.

Performance and telemetry: 
- Measured ~20% median reduction in fastpath end-to-end time on small change PRs where full integration tests were previously run unnecessarily.
- Telemetry hooks added to emit stage durations and suppression counts to the CI metrics pipeline (metric names: ci.sequencer.stage.duration, ci.dep_cleaner.suppressed_count).

Merge notes: 
- PR was squashed on merge. Final merge commit includes cleaned changelog and docs update. All reviewers approved. CI green on final run.

Follow-ups (short list): 
- ENG-10214: Add a small dashboard to visualize suppression trends per repo (tracked in linked_linear).
- ENG-9213: Explore moving heavier presubmit orchestration into a staged worker model if sequencer proves effective.

If you want to reproduce locally: see docs/ci/fastpath.md for running sequencer against local changes; tools/dep_signal_cleaner.py has a --dry-run mode that emits the delta without suppressing alerts.
